newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Silicon Graphics sees strong fiscal 1998.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Silicon Graphics sees strong fiscal 1998.

text.p: Silicon Graphics Inc chief executive Edward McCracken said the company's emphasis on improving its business processes will help it deliver a greater percentage of profits to the bottom line in fiscal 1998.

McCracken told Reuters in an interview after the company reported fourth quarter results the company expects it can sustain its fourth quarter gross margin levels of 49 percent in fiscal 1998 and "10 percent plus" operating profit rates.
The chairman and chief executive officer said he expects revenues to grow in the "mid-teens" for fiscal 1998.

"What we saw here was a significant increase in gross margins in the fourth quarter," said McCracken, noting that the 49 percent gross margin in the final quarter was five percentage points higher than its prior-year historical basis.

"We think that's sustainable next year, which is very, very positive news for us and the investors in our company," he said. "We think that can be turned into 10 percent-plus operating profit rates for the year for fiscal 1998.
"We think that (revenue) growth rates can be sustained as well, at least in the mid-teens," he added.

This would be lower than the 25 percent growth to $3.7 billion that Silicon Graphics reported in the fiscal year ended June 30, but a substantial increase from the seven percent revenue growth rate when 1996 revenues for Cray Research, which was acquired in April 1996, are included on a pro forma basis.
Silicon Graphics earlier beat Wall Street's fourth quarter earnings estimates by a wide margin -- reporting $0.56 a share profit compared with a First Call consensus of $0.34 a share.
Shares of Silicon Graphics, which have been weighed down by the company's troubled performance over a period of more than a year, jumped to $23 after hours from its close of $19-7/16.

McCracken said he expected analysts' estimates for fiscal year ending June 30, 1998 earnings -- which had been at a consensus of $1.31 a share according to a recent First Call survey -- to increase based on the company's outlook.

McCracken declined to discuss estimates, but said based on general comments in an conference call with analysts "we gave some guidance to the financial community this afternoon. That guidance I think would result in the numbers going up."
One analyst said after the call McCracken's comments were received as upbeat but cautious. The analyst said he expected consensus estimates to rise to around $1.45 a share.

Silicon Graphics's McCracken also said the company expects to take a $20 million charge in the first quarter of fiscal 1998 related to acquisition of ParaGraph International, a company which makes three-dimensional Internet software.

Silicon Graphics had announced an agreement to acquire ParaGraph, which has research and development facilities in California and Moscow, two months ago but had not disclosed the extend of any writeoffs it expected to make.
McCracken said the company expects to be cash flow positive for fiscal 1998, adding that the fourth quarter results were a welcome turnround after a "tough...very challenging year."

"It's a result of a lot of the things we've been working on over the last year, including the completion of the product transition, a lot of good execution and process improvements in the company," he said. "I think a lot of it also comes from the fact that we are now through this difficult, major product transition where we've changed every product in the company in a major way over the last 12 months."
McCracken said the company aims for backlog, which was at $537 million at June 30, to be in the $300-$500 million range.
Operating margins for the company, including Cray, were 3.1 percent fiscal 1997 and 4.2 percent in fiscal 1996.
